'''International relations'''
*[[Morocco–Spain relations]]
**[[2026 Morocco–Spain border incident]]
***[[Ceuta]]n [[Mayor-President of Ceuta|mayor-president]] [[Juan Jesús Vivas]] says that around 60,000 [[Illegal immigration|undocumented migrants]] have entered the [[Spain|Spanish]] exclave in [[North Africa]] in the last 24 hours, as the death toll rises to 57. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/jul/31/cueta-spain-morocco-italy-migration-schengen-europe-latest-news-updates#top-of-blog (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2kp639yx4o (BBC News)]
***Videos on [[social media]] appear to show the [[Spanish Army]] deploying military vehicles towards [[Morocco–Spain border|the border]] with [[Morocco]]. [https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/spain-spanish-army-seen-moving-toward-ceuta-border-with-morocco/ (Reuters)]
***[[France|French]] [[Minister of the Interior (France)|interior minister]] [[Laurent Nuñez]] announces that he has ordered increased controls at [[France–Spain border|the border]] with Spain amid fears the thousands of migrants entering Ceuta could make their way to France. [https://www.politico.eu/article/ceuta-crisis-migration-france-spain-border-checks-schengen-unity-morocco/ (''Politico'')]
***[[Austria]]n [[Chancellor of Austria|chancellor]] [[Christian Stocker]] and [[Finland|Finnish]] [[Minister of the Interior (Finland)|interior minister]] [[Mari Rantanen]] join [[Italy|Italian]] [[Prime Minister of Italy|prime minister]] [[Giorgia Meloni]] in calling for Spain to be suspended from the [[Schengen Area]] in response to the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta over the last 24 hours.  [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/finland-austria-join-italys-call-for-schengen-border-closures-after-mass-migrant-arrivals-in-spains-ceuta/4015081 (AA)]
***Spanish authorities close the [[Melilla]] [[Border control|border crossing]] with Morocco after around 400 migrants stormed the [[border barrier]]. [[RTVE]] reports the sound of gunfire and explosions. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/spain-closes-melilla-border-crossing-with-morocco-after-mass-entry-attempt/4014629 (AA)]
***Italy suspends Schengen [[Freedom of movement|border-free]] travel with Spain, introducing [[Border control|checks]] on air and sea passengers and strengthening controls with France along the [[France–Italy border]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/italy-suspends-eu-schengen-free-travel-pact-with-spain-over-ceuta-crisis-2026-07-31/ (Reuters)]
***[[Ministry of the Interior (Spain)|Spain's interior ministry]] says authorities have returned about 48,300 of roughly 50,000 migrants who entered Ceuta from Morocco. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spain-ceuta-morocco-migrants-border-crossings/ (CBS News)]
*[[Belarus–Latvia relations]]
**[[Latvia]] announces the sudden closure of [[Belarus–Latvia border|its border]] with [[Belarus]], citing "technical reasons". [https://www.reuters.com/world/latvia-closes-border-with-belarus-interior-minister-says-2026-07-31/ (Reuters)]

**[[Murder of Mir Raza Ali]]

[[Law enforcement in Pakistan|Police]] launch a murder investigation into the case. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2621007/kidnapped-man-found-murdered-in-jauhar (''The Express Tribune'')]
*[[2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings]]
**A [[Sri Lanka]]n [[Judiciary of Sri Lanka|court]] sentences former [[Sri Lanka Police|police]] [[Inspector General of Police (Sri Lanka)|chief]] [[Pujith Jayasundara]] to [[Capital punishment in Sri Lanka|death]] for [[negligence]] in failing to prevent the 2019 [[Easter]] bombings, which killed 279 people. Sri Lanka has not carried out an execution since 1976. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/2026/07/31/sri-lanka-sentences-ex-police-chief-to-death-over-2019-bombings#goog_rewarded (AFP via ''The Star'')]

*[[List of 2030 FIFA World Cup controversies|2030 FIFA World Cup controversies]]
**[[Carlos Cordeiro]], senior [[FIFA]] executive and adviser to [[List of presidents of FIFA|FIFA president]] [[Gianni Infantino]], resigns in protest of Infantino's plans to sell stakes in [[FIFA Forward Enterprise]] to private investors, including American banking institution [[JPMorgan Chase]], calling them "a bad deal for FIFA's members, a bad deal for [[Association football|football]], and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game". **Infantino reverses his plan to sell stakes in the [[FIFA World Cup]] amidst backlash. [https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49500782/fifa-world-cup-investment-private-gianni-infantino (ESPN)]
